models.description:
Model Summary: EfficientNet-B0 fine-tuned for binary Tuberculosis detection from chest X-rays. Trained on 16,807 Indian patient images from the ICMR-NIRT national TB prevalence survey (2019-2021). Achieves 87.3% validation accuracy. Input: 512×512 RGB chest X-ray. Output: TB Positive or Normal with confidence score.

Usage: import torch; from torchvision import models; import torch.nn as nn; model = models.efficientnet_b0(weights=None); model.classifier = nn.Sequential(nn.Dropout(0.3), nn.Linear(1280, 2)); model.load_state_dict(torch.load('tb_epoch_17.pth', map_location='cpu')); model.eval(). Input: 512×512 RGB chest X-ray normalized with ImageNet stats. Output: [TB_probability, Normal_probability].

System: Standalone binary classification model. Input: 512×512 chest X-ray in JPEG/PNG format. Output: Probability scores for TB Positive and Normal classes. No downstream dependencies.

Implementation Requirements: Training on Kaggle Notebook with Tesla T4 GPU (15GB VRAM), PyTorch 2.10. Training time approximately 5 minutes per epoch, 20 epochs total (about 1.5 hours). Inference works on CPU or GPU, approximately 50ms per image on CPU. Model size is 16 MB with 5.3M parameters.

Model Initialization: Fine-tuned from EfficientNet-B0 pre-trained on ImageNet. Classifier head replaced with Dropout(0.3) + Linear(1280, 2).

Model Stats: Size 16 MB, 5,309,282 parameters, 237 layers, input size 512×512×3, inference time approximately 50ms per image on CPU. No pruning, quantization, or differential privacy techniques applied.

Training Data: Source is IN-CXR (ICMR–National Institute for Research in Tuberculosis) from the National TB Prevalence Survey conducted door-to-door across all Indian states (2019-2021). Pre-processing included DICOM to JPEG conversion, 512×512 resize, and ImageNet normalization. Train/Val split is 80% (13,445 images) / 20% (3,362 images). Classes: TB Positive (8,232) and Normal (8,575). Data represents pan-India population across all states and union territories, covering diverse demographics, geographies, and equipment types.

Evaluation Results: Best model at Epoch 17 with 87.3% validation accuracy (93.6% training accuracy). Starting accuracy was 75.4% at Epoch 1. Evaluated on 20% hold-out validation set with no overlap with training data.

Usage Limitations: Trained only on Indian population chest X-rays. Binary classification only (TB/Normal) and cannot subtype TB. Not validated for pediatric use. Should be used as a screening tool, not primary diagnosis. Performance may vary on X-rays from different equipment manufacturers.

Ethics: Dataset sourced from government public health survey with appropriate consent. Model intended to assist, not replace, radiologist diagnosis. False negatives could delay TB treatment and should be confirmed with clinical evaluation. False positives could cause unnecessary anxiety and should be confirmed with sputum test.
